name: Mordecai and Esther
charge: Mordecai: bowing not to Haman. Esther: going in to the king against the law, after three days' fast: if I perish, I perish
summary: A Jew in the king's gate would not bow to an Agagite, and the Agagite bought a decree to kill every Jew in the empire. His cousin the queen fasted three days with all the Jews of Shushan and went in to the king uncalled. Haman was hanged on his own gallows, the Jews were given the day, and Mordecai was next unto the king. The feast of Purim keeps it.
offense: All the king's servants bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence; for he had told them that he was a Jew. Esther: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish. Mordecai's word to her: who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
judgment: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king's wrath pacified. The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed. The Greek Esther adds Mordecai's dream and the Lord's answer: the Lord hath done wonders for his people.

entries.commentary: After these things the king promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite and set his seat above all the princes, and all the king's servants in the king's gate bowed and reverenced him, for the king had so commanded, but Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence. The servants asked daily why Mordecai transgressed the king's commandment, and he hearkened not, but told them he was a Jew, and they told Haman to see whether Mordecai's matter would stand. We do not bow, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High. -

When Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence, he was full of wrath, and thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone once they had shown him the people of Mordecai. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai, not one man only. Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom's hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, seeking to erase us out of history.

In the first month, Nisan, in the twelfth year of the king, they cast Pur, that is the lot, before Haman from day to day and month to month, to the twelfth month, Adar. Haman told the king there was a certain people scattered abroad whose laws were diverse from all people and who kept not the king's laws, and it was not for the king's profit to suffer them, offering ten thousand talents of silver to have them destroyed. The king took his ring and gave it to Haman the Jews' enemy, granting him the silver and the people to do as he pleased. This is putting a hit out on the entire nation of Israel.

On the thirteenth day of the first month the king's scribes wrote according to all Haman commanded, to the king's lieutenants, governors and rulers of every province in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring. Letters were sent by posts to destroy, kill and cause to perish all Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, and to take the spoil for prey. The copy was published in every province so they should be ready, and the king and Haman sat down to drink while the city Shushan was perplexed.

When Mordecai perceived all that was done he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the midst of the city and cried with a loud and bitter cry, and came before the king's gate, for none might enter it clothed with sackcloth. In every province where the king's commandment and decree came there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. Imagine a decree today to kill every descendant of Israel, and you begin to feel what they went through.

Esther's maids and chamberlain told her, and the queen was exceedingly grieved and sent raiment to clothe Mordecai and take away his sackcloth, but he received it not. She sent Hatach, appointed to attend her, to learn what it was and why. Mordecai told Hatach all that had happened and of the money Haman promised to pay for the Jews to be destroyed, and gave him a copy of the decree published in Shushan to show Esther, charging her to go in to the king and make supplication for her people.

Esther answered by Hatach that all the king's servants and people knew that whosoever came unto the king in the inner court uncalled, man or woman, there was one law, to be put to death, except the king held out the golden sceptre that he may live. She said she had not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days, and they told Mordecai her words. She made an excuse, though she was the queen the king had chosen and loved above all the women.

Mordecai sent answer that Esther should not think she would escape in the king's house more than all the Jews, for if she altogether held her peace at this time, then enlargement and deliverance would arise to the Jews from another place, but she and her father's house would be destroyed. Who knoweth whether Esther was come to the kingdom for such a time as this. She was put in her position to serve this very purpose, and the deliverance of Israel cannot be held back; she would either help it along or be left behind while it came another way.

Esther returned answer that Mordecai should gather all the Jews in Shushan to fast for her, neither eating nor drinking three days, night or day, and she and her maidens would fast likewise, and so she would go in unto the king not according to the law, and if she perished, she perished. So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people. -

On the third day Esther put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court of the king's house over against the king's house, and the king sat on his royal throne over against the gate. When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtained favour in his sight, and he held out to her the golden sceptre in his hand, and Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre. She was not called by name, yet as soon as he saw her he received her, for a daughter of Israel finds favour in the eyes of a man.

The king asked what would Esther the queen and what was her request, offering even to the half of the kingdom, and Esther asked that the king and Haman come that day to a banquet she had prepared. The king said cause Haman to make haste that he may do as Esther said, so the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared. When a woman he loves prepares a table for him, the king bends to hear her every request.

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther's petition and request, to the half of the kingdom, and Esther answered that if she had found favour and it pleased the king, let the king and Haman come again to the banquet she would prepare on the morrow, and she would do as the king had said. The book of Esther shows both sides, the good side of a woman doing what she should and the wicked side of what she should not, so it puts a check on the spirit that rises up in women to rebel.

Haman went forth that day joyful and glad of heart, but when he saw Mordecai in the king's gate who stood not up nor moved for him, he was full of indignation, yet refrained himself and went home and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife. Haman told them of the glory of his riches, his many children, and all the ways the king had advanced him above the princes, and that Esther had let no man come to the banquet with the king but himself, and he was bidden again on the morrow. Yet all this availed him nothing so long as he saw Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate. Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends counselled that a gallows fifty cubits high be made, and on the morrow he should speak to the king that Mordecai be hanged thereon, and then go merrily to the banquet, and the thing pleased Haman and he caused the gallows to be made. It was the wife's idea, for the enemy's women are in cahoots with the work against Israel. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

At the banquet of wine the king again asked Esther her petition, promising it would be granted even to the half of the kingdom. Esther pleaded for her life and the life of her people, for they had been sold to be destroyed, slain, and to perish, and had it been only bondage she would have held her tongue. The king demanded to know who he was that dared presume in his heart to do such a thing.

Esther named the adversary and enemy as this wicked Haman, and Haman was afraid before the king and the queen. Sitting at the table, Haman could hardly eat, for he had just arrayed Mordecai and just heard his own household warn him he would fall before the Jews, and now he was exposed at the dinner table.

The king rose in his wrath and went into the palace garden, and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther, seeing that evil was determined against him. When the king returned, Haman had fallen upon the bed where Esther was, and the king took it as an assault on the queen in his own house. As the word went out of the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

Harbonah, a chamberlain, told the king of the gallows fifty cubits high that Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standing at Haman's house. The king commanded Haman be hanged on it, and they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's wrath was pacified. This is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how He moves.

That day the king gave the house of Haman, the Jews' enemy, to Esther, and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her. The king took off the ring he had taken from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman. Everything Haman had was given to Mordecai.

Esther fell down at the king's feet and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite and the device he had devised against the Jews. The king held out the golden scepter, and Esther rose and asked that letters be written to reverse the letters Haman devised to destroy the Jews in all the provinces. She asked how she could endure to see the evil that would come upon her people and the destruction of her kindred.

The king told Esther and Mordecai that he had given Esther the house of Haman and had hanged Haman for laying hand upon the Jews. He granted them to write for the Jews in the king's name and seal it with the king's ring, for a writing sealed with the king's ring could no man reverse. Esther and Mordecai were given the king's authority, so the reputation and word of the king stood behind whatever they wrote.

The king's scribes were called in the third month, Sivan, on the twenty-third day, and it was written to the Jews, lieutenants, deputies, and rulers of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, a hundred twenty and seven provinces, each in its own writing and language. This is the span of the Persian empire, and Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity, which shows we have history in these lands. -

The king granted the Jews in every city to gather, stand for their life, and destroy any power that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil. Everyone who had listened to Haman's proclamation to kill the Jews was now subject to the Jews' revenge upon their enemies. The decree was to be ready upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, the day the Jews would avenge themselves, for nothing pacifies the Most High but vengeance on the enemies of His people. The posts rode out hastened on mules, camels, and dromedaries by the king's commandment.

Mordecai went out from the king in royal apparel of blue and white, a great crown of gold, and a garment of fine linen and purple, and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad. The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor, and in every province and city where the decree came they had a feast and a good day. Many of the people of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews fell upon them, a picture of the future when the fear of Israel will be on all nations and they will serve the Most High.

In the twelfth month Adar, on the thirteenth day, when the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, it was turned to the contrary and the Jews had rule over those that hated them. The Jews gathered in their cities, and no man could withstand them, for the fear of them fell upon all people, and the rulers, lieutenants, deputies, and officers helped the Jews because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them. Mordecai was great in the king's house and his fame went throughout all the provinces, and this man waxed greater and greater. Though Esther was queen, she was still subject to Mordecai, the man of Israel who wrote the edict.

The Jews smote all their enemies with the sword, slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would to those that hated them. In Shushan the palace they slew and destroyed five hundred men, and they slew the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. On the spoil they laid not their hands.

The number slain in Shushan was brought before the king, who told Esther the Jews had slain five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman, and asked what more she desired. Esther asked that the Jews in Shushan be granted the next day also according to the decree, and that Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows. The king commanded it done, and the Jews in Shushan gathered on the fourteenth day and slew three hundred more, but on the spoil they laid not their hands.

The other Jews in the king's provinces gathered, stood for their lives, had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, laying not their hands on the prey. This was on the thirteenth day of Adar, and on the fourteenth they rested and made a day of feasting and gladness. The Jews of Shushan rested on the fifteenth day, so the Jews of the unwalled towns made the fourteenth a day of gladness, feasting, and sending portions one to another. This is where the gift giving of Purim comes from.

Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews near and far to establish that they keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar yearly. These were the days the Jews rested from their enemies, the month turned from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day. They were to make them days of feasting, joy, sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor. This is where the feast of Purim comes from, a feast that commemorates the destruction of Israel's enemies.

The Jews undertook to keep what Mordecai wrote, because Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite had devised against the Jews to destroy them and had cast Pur, that is the lot, to consume them. Pur was the Persian custom of casting lots, much like the lot cast for Jonah to see whose fault the storm was. When Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that Haman's wicked device return upon his own head, and that he and his sons be hanged on the gallows. -

These days were called Purim after the name Pur, and the Jews ordained and took upon themselves and their seed to keep these two days every year. The days were to be remembered and kept throughout every generation, family, province, and city. These days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews nor the memorial of them perish from their seed, which shows Israel still celebrates Purim today.

Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim. Letters were sent to all the Jews in the hundred twenty and seven provinces with words of peace and truth, to confirm the days of Purim in their appointed times. The decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book, which is Israel's own book of history. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

The king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land and upon the isles of the sea, and all the acts of his power and might, with the declaration of the greatness of Mardocheus whereunto the king advanced him, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia. Mardocheus the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, great among the Jews and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed. The Feast of Purim has now been established, and Mardocheus is lifted up to be number two in the kingdom for the works he did to warn the king and for standing with Esther through everything that led to this day.

At Rephidim there was no water, and the people did chide with Moses: wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? At the first sign of trial the people jumped off the Lord's bandwagon again, the same as we do today when tribulation comes. Moses cried unto the Lord, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me. They were ready to kill the prophet over water, blaming the brother for what only the Most High controls; we have to build our faith up like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who trusted the Lord even when trials came.

The Lord stood before Moses upon the rock in Horeb; Moses smote the rock, and water came out of it in the sight of the elders of Israel. He called the place Massah and Meribah, temptation and chiding, because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not? That is wickedness: He had just made Egypt dark, slain their firstborn, and sent His angel in the chariot to guide us, and the people still asked whether He was with them. The mercy of the Most High in bearing that is beyond us.

Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. Amalek was the first nation to come against Israel after Egypt; Amalek was Esau's grandson, born to Eliphaz of Timna the concubine, a duke in the land of Edom. When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today. The sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in: Moses is the man to hearken to, so do not speak against him. And Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword; Joshua was a mighty warrior even then.

Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. Moses wrote it, and [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25) is that rehearsal: remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way. Amalek smote the hindmost, all that were feeble, when Israel was faint and weary, and he feared not God. He did not meet the mighty men in the front; he went to the back to slay the women, the children, and the old ones. That same spirit works against the nation's young and old today. The Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation. By the time Moses rehearsed it in Deuteronomy, forty years had passed and the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves; hundreds of years after that the Lord sent Saul by Samuel to smite Amalek for what was done coming out of Egypt. God be true and every man a liar: the nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed. Saul did not finish Agag's line, and in Esther's day Haman the Agagite of that same seed rose against Israel; the war truly runs from generation to generation. Today that seed says they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan, robbing Israel of identity and prospering off the oppression. The Lord says He will make them come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. The whole world is set up between Jacob and Esau, and Esau is the end of this world, the so-called white man, with Amalek leading; it is not speaking of the Arab man, for if Ishmael had a rulership still to come, Israel would have another captivity to enter, and Christ has already redeemed us from the curse of the law. The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

verses.text: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.
And all the king’s servants, that were in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.
Then the king’s servants, which were in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?
Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew.
And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.

And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.
Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king’s house, more than all the Jews.

For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
Then Esther bade them return Mordecai this answer,

Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on her royal apparel, and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, over against the king’s house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.

And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what is thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half of the kingdom.
So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? and it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.
Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:

For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king’s damage.
Then the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?
And Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath went into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.
So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.
On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews’ enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.
And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.
Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,

And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the king’s provinces:
For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?

Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.

Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.

And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.

And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.
And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,
To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.
And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;
Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,

The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their appointed time every year;

And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.
And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.

And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
Then Mardocheus said, God hath done these things.
For I remember a dream which I saw concerning these matters, and nothing thereof hath failed.
A little fountain became a river, and there was light, and the sun, and much water: this river is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen:
And the two dragons are I and Aman.
And the nations were those that were assembled to destroy the name of the Jews:

And my nation is this Israel, which cried to God, and were saved: for the Lord hath saved his people, and the Lord hath delivered us from all those evils, and God hath wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
Therefore hath he made two lots, one for the people of God, and another for all the Gentiles.
And these two lots came at the hour, and time, and day of judgment, before God among all nations.
So God remembered his people, and justified his inheritance.

Therefore those days shall be unto them in the month Adar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with an assembly, and joy, and with gladness before God, according to the generations for ever among his people.
For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

text.text: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that were with him.
And all the king’s servants, that were in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.
Then the king’s servants, which were in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?
Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew.
And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.

And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.
Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king’s house, more than all the Jews.

For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
Then Esther bade them return Mordecai this answer,

Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on her royal apparel, and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, over against the king’s house: and the king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, over against the gate of the house.

And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.
Then said the king unto her, What wilt thou, queen Esther? and what is thy request? it shall be even given thee to the half of the kingdom.
So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee: and what is thy request? and it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.
Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request:

For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not countervail the king’s damage.
Then the king Ahasuerus answered and said unto Esther the queen, Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?
And Esther said, The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath went into the palace garden: and Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman was fallen upon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the king, Will he force the queen also before me in the house? As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

And Harbonah, one of the chamberlains, said before the king, Behold also, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.
So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the king’s wrath pacified.
On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews’ enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.
And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.
And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews.
Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,

And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the king’s provinces:
For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?

Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews.

Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.

And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour.

And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.
And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,
To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.
And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them;
Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them,

The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their appointed time every year;

And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.
And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea.

And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
Then Mardocheus said, God hath done these things.
For I remember a dream which I saw concerning these matters, and nothing thereof hath failed.
A little fountain became a river, and there was light, and the sun, and much water: this river is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen:
And the two dragons are I and Aman.
And the nations were those that were assembled to destroy the name of the Jews:

And my nation is this Israel, which cried to God, and were saved: for the Lord hath saved his people, and the Lord hath delivered us from all those evils, and God hath wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
Therefore hath he made two lots, one for the people of God, and another for all the Gentiles.
And these two lots came at the hour, and time, and day of judgment, before God among all nations.
So God remembered his people, and justified his inheritance.

Therefore those days shall be unto them in the month Adar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with an assembly, and joy, and with gladness before God, according to the generations for ever among his people.
For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
